ALGER, 06/07/2026 (Algeria Tech) — Le mi: ALGIERS, 07/06/2026 (Algeria Tech) — The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Sid Ali Zerrouki, represented Algeria at the first Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance, organized under the auspices of the United Nations. The event focused on the transition from theoretical principles to concrete mechanisms, including technology transfer, capacity building, and bridging the digital divide.
Participation active de l'Algérie aux en: Algeria's active participation in international AI issues
Le ministre de la Poste et des Télécommu: The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Sid Ali Zerrouki, took part in the first Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance, organized under the auspices of the United Nations in Geneva from July 2 to 4, 2026. This historic event brought together representatives from over 150 countries, private sector experts, and international organizations to discuss regulatory frameworks and concrete mechanisms aimed at guiding the development and use of AI. According to the organizers, Algeria played a proactive role by advocating for a balanced approach between innovation, ethics, and technological sovereignty.
Lors de son intervention, Sid Ali Zerrou: During his speech, Sid Ali Zerrouki emphasized the importance of international cooperation to ensure equitable access to AI technologies, particularly in developing countries. He also discussed ongoing national initiatives to integrate AI into both the public and private sectors, focusing on local skills training and technology transfer. These commitments are part of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, adopted in 2024, which aims to position Algeria as a key player in emerging technologies in Africa.
Analyse et enjeux pour l'Algérie : souve: Analysis and challenges for Algeria: technological sovereignty and competitiveness
La participation de l'Algérie à ce dialo: Algeria's participation in this international dialogue is part of a broader dynamic to modernize its information and communication technology (ICT) sector. The country has embarked on an ambitious digital transformation plan, with a budget of 1,200 billion dinars (approximately 8.5 billion euros) allocated through 2030. This plan includes the deployment of 5G networks across all 58 wilayas by 2027, as well as the development of innovation ecosystems in strategic areas such as AI, cybersecurity, and quantum computing.
Sur le plan économique, l'intégration de: On the economic front, AI integration could generate productivity gains estimated at 15% in the industrial, healthcare, and public services sectors, according to a recent study by the National Agency for Investment Promotion (ANDI). However, major challenges persist, notably the shortage of qualified local skills, estimated at over 50,000 unfilled positions by 2028, and the need to strengthen public-private partnerships to accelerate the adoption of these technologies. These issues highlight the urgency of a coherent strategy to make Algeria a regional technology hub.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien : entre: Context of the Algerian ICT sector: between ambition and realities
Le secteur des TIC en Algérie connaît un: The ICT sector in Algeria is experiencing sustained growth, with a mobile penetration rate exceeding 125% in 2025, according to the latest data from the Postal and Electronic Communications Regulatory Authority (ARPCE). This rate places Algeria among the most advanced African countries in terms of connectivity, with over 62 million mobile subscribers and 32 million internet users, including 20 million on fixed and mobile broadband. These figures reflect the efforts made by national operators, namely Algérie Télécom, Mobilis, and Djezzy, to expand network coverage and improve connection speeds.
Dans ce cadre, le plan numérique 2030 vi: In this context, the Digital Plan 2030 aims to achieve a 90% 5G coverage rate and an average speed of 100 Mbps by 2027. To achieve this, the state has allocated 450 billion dinars (approximately 3.2 billion euros) to modernize infrastructure, including 200 billion dedicated to deploying fiber optics in remote wilayas. Furthermore, the ARPCE launched a special 5 billion dinar fund in 2025 to support local startups in the fields of AI, fintech, and the Internet of Things (IoT). These initiatives are accompanied by legislative reform aimed at further liberalizing the telecommunications market and attracting foreign investment.
Le ministre de la Poste et des Télécommu: The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Sid Ali Zerrouki, stated at the end of the dialogue: "Algeria reaffirms its commitment to inclusive and responsible governance of artificial intelligence. Our participation in this international forum demonstrates our willingness to actively contribute to the development of global standards that reflect the realities and aspirations of developing countries."
De son côté, le directeur général de l'A: For his part, the Director General of ARPCE, Mohamed El Amine Hamdani, emphasized: "The discussions held in Geneva confirmed the importance of international cooperation to overcome technological and regulatory challenges. Algeria, thanks to its infrastructure and human capital, is well-positioned to play a leading role in this field."
La prochaine étape pour l'Algérie consis: The next step for Algeria will be to finalize the National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence, scheduled for adoption in the first quarter of 2027. This document, currently in the validation phase, will define sectoral priorities, funding mechanisms, and international partnerships necessary to realize the country's ambitions. At the same time, the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications announced the launch of a national AI training program, in collaboration with universities and research centers, to train 10,000 specialists by 2030.
Sur le plan international, l'Algérie env: On the international stage, Algeria plans to join the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI), an initiative bringing together 29 countries and the European Union to promote ethical and inclusive AI. This membership, expected by the end of the year, would allow Algeria to benefit from funding and technology transfers while consolidating its position on the global stage.
